summary: A thin day: Reddit, Bluesky and X were unreachable, so only Hacker News (this week's comments and Ask HN posts) could be mined, and only two complaints had enough independent, verifiable sources. Developers are being locked out of GitHub with no notice or support, and people can't curate or share a slop-free YouTube feed without Google Takeout hacks.

ideas.title: Repo Lifeboat
ideas.oneLiner: Continuous off-GitHub mirror of all your repos, issues and PRs, plus an appeal tracker for when your account is suspended.
ideas.problem: Developers are having GitHub accounts suspended or locked with no notice and a ticket-only support path that can go unanswered for months. Their code, issues and paid orgs become unreachable overnight, and the existing backup tools are CLI scripts people set up only after it's too late.
ideas.targetUsers: Solo developers, freelancers, students and small teams whose whole work history lives in one GitHub account.
ideas.monetization: Free for 5 repos; $4/month personal plan for unlimited repos with scheduled mirrors to your own S3/R2/Backblaze bucket; $15/month team plan.
mvp: Connect GitHub with a read-only token and pick repos/orgs to protect
Scheduled incremental mirror of git data, issues, PR discussions and wikis to your own S3/R2 bucket or a Forgejo/Codeberg instance
One-click restore export: bundle that can be pushed to another forge
Account-health check that emails you if the token starts failing (a likely sign of suspension)
Appeal tracker with the support URLs and a timestamped checklist/template for reinstatement tickets

competitors.name: python-github-backup
competitors.gap: A command-line tool: issues and PR details are opt-in flags, private repos need token setup, and scheduling (cron/CI) is left to the user, so most people don't have it running before a lockout.

competitors.name: Forgejo/Gitea pull mirrors
competitors.gap: Mirror git data only, require running your own server, and don't carry issues or PR discussions in a restorable form.

sources.title: Ask HN: What to do about incorrectly suspended GitHub account, no notice?

ideas.title: Curated YouTube Feed Builder
ideas.oneLiner: Build a chronological, algorithm-free feed from a shareable list of channels, with no Google Takeout dance.
ideas.problem: People can't stop the YouTube homepage from feeding them slop, and the alternatives are awkward: sharing a subscription list means exporting via Google Takeout, and curated-feed projects lack basics like recency sorting or a TV app.
ideas.targetUsers: Tech and niche-interest viewers who watch a small set of channels, and curators who want to share a channel list with friends or a community.
ideas.monetization: Free for up to 50 channels; $3/month for unlimited channels, watch-later sync and a TV-friendly view; optional paid public curated lists.
mvp: Paste channel URLs or upload a Takeout/OPML/CSV file to create a list
Chronological feed with upload-date, duration and type filters
Shareable link for a channel list that others can clone in one click
Sort by recency and hide Shorts
Responsive layout usable on a TV browser (Apple TV/Android TV) as a first step toward native apps

competitors.name: FreeTube / NewPipe
competitors.gap: Subscriptions move only via export files (CSV/OPML) between apps, it is install-per-device with no shareable curated list, and Google's export format changes have broken imports before.

competitors.name: HackerTube
competitors.gap: A single fixed curation (HN-recommended videos) rather than a tool to build your own feed; commenters asked for recency sorting and an Apple TV app.
